nom: Timeless Skin Care Vitamin C Serum with Vitamin E & Ferulic Acid - Brightening Serum - for Oily & Dry Skin - Fragrance-F

segments.dry: One reviewer who leans dry found her skin became drier and her fine lines more pronounced after switching to this 20% formula from a 15% version, while another with dry, sensitive, rosacea-prone skin reports no irritation and some healing.
segments.combination: A reviewer with combination skin, describing both oily and dry zones, reports the serum works well across both without stinging or pilling.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers are divided: several report no irritation even with rosacea, dryness, or acne-proneness, while others caution that the 20% concentration can sting broken skin or burn when applied to the neck and chest even though the face tolerates it fine.
segments.normal: A reviewer with normal-to-dry skin reports no stinging or irritation, smoother and brighter skin, and fewer lingering post-acne marks with consistent use.
segments.mature: Older reviewers, including several in their 50s, 60s, and 70s, report brighter, smoother, more youthful-looking skin, with one describing considerably reduced wrinkles.

concerns.aging: Reviewers using it as part of an anti-aging routine, several in their 50s to 70s, report brighter, more even, more youthful-looking skin, with one describing considerably reduced wrinkles and another linking it to a subtle plumping effect when paired with a derma roller.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers describe the texture as hydrating or at least non-drying, but one reviewer who leans dry found her skin became drier and her fine lines more pronounced after moving from a 15% to this 20% concentration, and another notes it can feel tight before moisturizer is applied.
concerns.redness: One reviewer with rosacea-prone skin reports it did not worsen her redness, though it also did not visibly reduce it.
concerns.barrier: Most reviewers, including several with sensitive or reactive skin, report no stinging or irritation; exceptions include stinging when applied over broken or popped skin, and burning when used on the neck and chest even though the same reviewer's face tolerated it fine.
concerns.spots: Many reviewers report fading of dark spots, sun spots, hyperpigmentation, acne scarring, or melasma with consistent use, though one reviewer says that after several months her hyperpigmentation has faded only slightly, if at all.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers report no new breakouts, with a couple describing fewer post-acne marks or soothed acne; one acne-prone, sensitive-skin reviewer says it did not react the way other serums have.
concerns.oiliness: One reviewer with combination skin, describing oily and dry zones, reports the serum performs well on the oilier areas without stinging or pilling; there is little other feedback specific to oil control.

Pump dispenser leaks, sprays, or is hard to use
Strong scent likened to hot dog water
Seen as strong value next to SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic
Single-use packets limit oxidation and pack well for travel

extraits.texte: Pic #2 - With my normal routine using SkinCeuticals of 6~ mo and Makeup Pic #1 - Using the timeless Vitamin C for like 2wks and Makeup So I normally use the SkinCeuticals Vitamin C (I buy mine off Ebay cause ain’t nobody got $180 to spend on 1oz of product) but ran out before I could order more and read this was a similar dupe for it. I’ve used at least 4 bottles of the SkinCeuticals, so I would say my skin is pretty used to the actives. This felt nice on my skin the first couple of days, but after about 2 weeks of using, my skin became dry with my fine lines around my eyes becoming so much more pronounced despite stopping the application on my cheeks. I do lean more on the dry skin side, but the SkinCeuticals formula does not dry me out in the same way. The big difference is that this is 20% vs the 15% my skin is used to, so I’m sure that plays a role in it. However - the scent is more pungent in a chemically way compared to SkinCeuticals and actually stings my skin if I have popped a pimple or itched my face during the day. I’m now basically doing skin barrier recovery and waiting for my SkinCeuticals order to be delivered, but might keep this handy for short term emergency situations.

extraits.titre: Fantastic vitamin c serum even for rosacea
extraits.texte: Fantastic vitamin C serum. I am actually mad at myself for waiting so long to buy this. Everything I've read said that vitamin c serum would likely irritate my extremely sensitive, dry, rosacea skin. Even my dermatologist told me this. So, I put off buying any for years. I finally decided to try it and it's fabulous! It doesn't irritate my skin and actually seems to be helping my skin heal. I used it every other day the first week and then every day thereafter. I noticed a difference in my skin after two weeks. It's smoother, softer and looks healthier/more radiant. I don't think it's helped the redness, but it definitely hasn't made it any worse. I've been using it now for about two months and am continuing to see improvements. I did separate the serum into two bottles (using a second, dark colored bottle I had for half of the serum) and have stored both bottles in the refrigerator. I haven't seen any signs of oxidation and next time I don't think I'll bother dividing the serum; I just don't think it's necessary. I do use it on my neck and chest as well as my face, so i think I'll use it up before three months anyway (timeless guarantees it for three months). Also, I have ph strips (bought them on Amazon) and test all my liquid cosmetics. This tested between 2 and 3 (see attached photo), so the ph is correct.

Love timeless vit c. It’s not oily at all and a little goes a long way. Super important to protect your skin from the harmful sun. Highly recommend. Would be careful using on neck and chest. I have sensitive skin and it burned me. I can tolerate on my face with no problem.

extraits.titre: My ride-or-die vitamin C - effective, gentle, and consistently great
extraits.texte: This is one of those products I keep coming back to and have repurchased monthly for years. Timeless Vitamin C has been a staple in my routine for a long time, and it is one of the main reasons my skin stays bright and even. The formula is straightforward and effective - 20% L-ascorbic acid with vitamin E and ferulic acid, no fragrance, no unnecessary fillers. The serum texture is very pleasant and lightweight, absorbs quickly, and layers well under the rest of my morning skincare and sunscreen. I’ve never experienced stinging, irritation, or sensitivity with this, even though my skin can be reactive if a vitamin C formula is poorly done. With consistent use, my skin looks clearer, more even-toned, and overall healthier. It helps keep post-acne marks from lingering and gives a noticeable brightness without feeling harsh or drying. A little goes a long way, and I appreciate that the ingredient list stays focused on proven actives rather than marketing extras. For reference, I have fair skin that is generally normal but leans dry in the winter, with a history of acne. I also use azelaic acid, retinoids, peptides, and hydrating serums in my routine, and this vitamin C plays very nicely with everything. If you’re looking for a no-nonsense, effective vitamin C that actually delivers results, this one has earned its permanent spot in my routine.

extraits.titre: Most amazing wrinkle remover I've ever tried.
extraits.texte: The wrinkles on my 73 yr old face have reduced considerably. I use every morning and night and keep it refrigerated. Miracle worker!! Love it so much.
I do have sensitive and acne prone skin. It didn't react at all like other serum.

Have been using Vanicream’s vitamin C serum for a year, but due to using estrogen based night cream even with using vitamin C and SPF I got a spot of melasma. This vitamin C serum is highly recommended on Reddit and the cost is very reasonable, so figured I’d give it a chance. Already liking the results. Melasma seems less prominent. Only downside is it does seem to make my day cream + makeup migrate into my eyes toward the end of the day. Worth it if my skin looks better.
